clue.text: Regular time when it gets dark?

blocks.note: first meaning: steady, uniform, level
second meaning: an archaic poetic word for dusk or nightfall

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one question about a fixed hour of nightfall, but it splits after the first word into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular rhythm is a steady one, and the archaic word for evening, as in 'eventide', is the same four letters.

clue.text: Insect destroying leaf

indicators.note: to destroy something is to break it apart, so the letters are smashed and rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden pest is chewing a leaf to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The leaf-eating bug suggests a caterpillar or aphid, but the four letters of the leaf itself are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This small jumping parasite is a wingless bloodsucking member of the insect class.

clue.text: Quiet animal to meander

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a river mammal

explanation.surface: A silent creature ambles about aimlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' is vague on purpose; the crossing letters and the musical P narrow it to a river mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter about is a mainly British idiom for wandering or pottering around in a leisurely, aimless way.

clue.text: Take prominent position and live below front of palace

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
in a down clue one thing below another is written after it in the column

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
to live somewhere is to reside there

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a grand role and moves into the palace.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'below' means the second piece follows the first, so the palace's initial sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to sit in authority over a meeting or court, occupying the chair of honour.

clue.text: A new girl in charge of a plant

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
gel is an upper-class British pronunciation of girl
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly hired young woman is put in charge of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory in the surface; here it is the botanical sense. GEL, the posh drawl of 'girl', is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is a tall aromatic herb whose candied green stems are used in cake decoration.

clue.text: Ways to show instructions

blocks.note: first meaning: routes or bearings, as in heading off in all ways
second meaning: guidance on how to do something

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests methods of displaying a manual; the two nouns either side of the link are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both compass bearings one may travel in and the step-by-step guidance printed on a packet.

clue.text: Fuel reeks with one getting ill

indicators.note: something falling ill is out of sorts, so these letters are disordered and set in a new pattern

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The smell of fuel is strong enough to make someone feel sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is both the verb and the number: eight letters together, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerosene is a light petroleum oil burned in lamps, heaters and jet engines; Britons call it paraffin.

clue.text: Bad person reviled, troubled about nothing

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and unsettled, so the letters are stirred into a new order
to be about something is to go around it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: taken as written
zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A wicked person, hated by all, is upset over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters of the past participle wrap around the round letter standing for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An evildoer is someone who commits wicked acts, a straightforward wrongdoer or villain.

clue.text: Is among those voting against, making nasty sounds

indicators.note: to be among a group is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: in Parliament the votes against are the noes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dissenter in a vote heckles loudly among the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: NOES is the plural of the 'no' vote, as in the Commons cry 'the noes have it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is an unpleasant or unwanted sound, so harsh racket in the plural fits.

clue.text: Child at home with female worker

blocks.note: someone at home is in
F is the abbreviation for female
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A youngster is at home with a woman who works there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is a crossword convention for a worker ant or bee.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child, a baby or toddler; British schools also use it for the youngest pupils.

clue.text: In good condition for match

blocks.note: first meaning: healthy and in shape
second meaning: to suit or correspond to

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an athlete ready for a game, and 'fit for match' makes it run together; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes physical health, while the verb means to suit or agree with something.

clue.text: To kneel's awkward — I'm bony!

definitions.note: a first-person riddle: the answer speaks of itself

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsy and out of shape, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone complains that kneeling is uncomfortable because they are so thin.
explanation.walkthrough: The speaker of the riddle is the answer itself, and the 'S of the contraction is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the framework of bones in a body, so it could say it is nothing but bone.

clue.text: Priest in some religion

indicators.note: some of a word is only part of it, so the letters lie inside the following word

blocks.note: letters two to four of the word

explanation.surface: A clergyman who belongs to a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the biblical priest who raised Samuel, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament book of Samuel, this man was high priest at the shrine of Shiloh.

clue.text: Little girl with the right to be indecisive

blocks.note: Di is the short form of Diana
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A small girl who is entitled to change her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little girl' means a girl's name made short, the standard crossword sense of 'little'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to hesitate nervously, unable to make up one's mind between choices.

clue.text: Note exclamation of annoyance

blocks.note: first meaning: the first degree of the sol-fa scale
second meaning: the cry made famous by Homer Simpson

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to jot down a grumble, but the musical syllable and the cartoon cry share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic sol-fa names the keynote with this syllable, and Homer Simpson's catchphrase spells it the same way when he errs.

clue.text: Attack the boss — a shark!

blocks.note: to hammer someone is to attack them hard
the head is the person in charge

explanation.surface: An office worker urges an assault on a predatory, ruthless manager.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation turns 'shark' into an insult for the boss; it is really the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This shark is named for its flattened, T-shaped head with an eye at each end.

clue.text: In seat I'd munched little cakes, maybe

indicators.note: food that is munched is chewed to bits, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sitting in my chair, I nibbled some small cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition placing the eater, but it is part of the fodder. 'Maybe' marks cakes as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainties are delicacies, small choice titbits of food such as fancy pastries.

clue.text: Peace or suffering round New York?

blocks.note: harm is damage or hurt
a round shape is the letter O
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A question of whether New York's neighbourhoods know calm or strife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a container signal; here it simply supplies the ring-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmony is agreement and concord between people, the opposite of conflict.

clue.text: It's ultra unusual to be a totally selfless person

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters leave their ordinary order

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: It is very rare to find anyone who thinks only of others.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder starts the clue, including the contracted verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An altruist acts out of concern for others' welfare with no thought of personal gain.

clue.text: Like clues characteristically identified

blocks.note: surface reading: how hints in a detective story are typically recognised
setter's reading: the way crossword clues are always labelled, each with its figure

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clues' suggests a detective spotting evidence; think instead of the puzzle in front of you, where every clue has a figure beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword clues are labelled by the figures in their grid squares, so the answer describes how they are tagged.

clue.text: Man with title in London borough, full of love

indicators.note: something full of a thing has it inside, so one piece is packed within another

blocks.note: Barnet is a borough of north London
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman living in a London suburb is deeply in love.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET is an outer London borough. Love meaning nil comes from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British rank below a baron, addressed as Sir.

clue.text: Rubbish piled up — or rocks piled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, piling up means stacking from the bottom, so the letters read upward

blocks.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish talk

explanation.surface: Either a heap of junk or a heap of stones.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase does two jobs: first it turns a word upside down in the column, then it describes the answer. A tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a craggy outcrop of stacked granite boulders on a hill, especially in south-west England.

clue.text: Demonstration in favour of experiment

blocks.note: pro means for
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A rally held in support of a scientific trial.
explanation.walkthrough: A march in favour of something sounds odd, since this kind of march is usually against something; the pieces simply join.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a public march or rally voicing objection, the same thing as this word.

clue.text: Banner seen when ship crosses river

indicators.note: to cross something is to straddle it, so one piece lies across and around another

blocks.note: a steamer is a steamship
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Flags are flown as a vessel makes its way over the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The river letter goes inside the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant flying from a mast, a kind of banner.

clue.text: Botanist ultimately needing plant sample

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: In the end a plant scientist must collect a specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sample' pretends to be a botanical specimen but means a small trial portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small portion given to try, a foretaste or trial helping.

clue.text: Archbishop once in place of worship

blocks.note: first meaning: the surname of a father and son who both became Archbishop of Canterbury
second meaning: a building for religious rites

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a former archbishop at prayer; the surname of two twentieth-century and Victorian archbishops is also a word for a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick and William were both leaders of the Church of England, and the common noun names a sacred building.

clue.text: The hotel left out a drink

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel forgot to serve someone their beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Hotel stands for H in the radio alphabet; take it from the article and add the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the hot drink brewed from dried leaves of the tea plant.

clue.text: Individual departed, leader deposed

indicators.note: a deposed leader is removed from the top, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: someone departed has gone

explanation.surface: A lone figure leaves after the ruler is overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first letter of the word for departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A single person or thing is one, as in 'every one of them'.

clue.text: His guest can become most effusive

indicators.note: becoming means changing into something else, so the letters turn into a new word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A host's visitor may turn out to be the most fulsome in praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening two words supply all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gushing talk overflows with enthusiasm, so the superlative describes the most effusive speaker.

clue.text: A Native American, second person seen as warlike?

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a hawk favours military action, the opposite of a dove

explanation.surface: A tribesman is described as the second warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is not an ordinal here: MO is British slang for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are an Iroquois people of New York State and Canada, a member of a Native American nation.

clue.text: Loathe that enemy? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only partly, so the letters are a fragment inside the words before

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A question about whether one fully detests a foe.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to feel intense dislike, which is the plain synonym.

clue.text: It could be ash — before or after burning

definitions.text: It could be ash — before or after burning

blocks.clueFragment: It could be ash — before or after burning
blocks.note: surface reading: a riddle about ash as the grey residue left by a fire

blocks.clueFragment: It could be ash — before or after burning
blocks.note: setter's reading: ash is a tree timber, and logs remain the same material whether lit or not

explanation.walkthrough: Ash means cinders in the surface, but it is also a tree; before burning that timber is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a hardwood tree whose timber is used for tool handles and firewood, so it is an example.

clue.text: Belongings in back of cottage, say

indicators.note: the back of a word is its tail, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
to say is to state

explanation.surface: Possessions kept at the rear of a country house, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is a verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's estate is all the property and possessions they own, especially when left at death.

clue.text: Something watery is what you want here!

blocks.note: first meaning: a liquid with something dissolved in it
second meaning: the answer the solver is looking for in this puzzle

explanation.walkthrough: The second half talks to the solver directly about the puzzle itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists call a liquid mixture with dissolved substances by this name, and it is also the answer to any problem.
